assumptions.choice: A selling-climax day is searched among the prior 1 through 10 trading days.
assumptions.reason: The specification gives a 5-10 day recent window but does not define one exact lookback length; 10 days uses the stated maximum window.

assumptions.choice: A sharp drop is defined as a one-day close-to-close decline of at least 5%.
assumptions.reason: The specification requires a sharp drop but provides no numerical threshold.

assumptions.choice: The most recent qualifying selling-climax day is used.
assumptions.reason: The specification does not specify how to choose when multiple days qualify.

assumptions.choice: Price confirmation is implemented as a bullish engulfing candle on the confirmation day.
assumptions.reason: The specification provides bullish engulfing as an explicit example and does not define a large-body threshold.

assumptions.choice: Sideways means the prior 20-day high-low range is at most 10% of its low; prolonged downtrend means the prior close is no higher than the close 10 days earlier; strong sustained uptrend means price is more than 10% above both the 200-day SMA and the close 20 days earlier.
assumptions.reason: These required qualitative filters have no stated numerical definitions.

assumptions.choice: The stop-loss is 2 ATR below executed entry price and take-profit is 2 times that risk above executed entry price.
assumptions.reason: Both choices are within the stated 1.5-2 ATR stop range and 1:2 to 1:3 reward range.

assumptions.choice: Position size is floored to the largest whole-share quantity whose 2-ATR stop loss equals no more than 1% of current portfolio value.
assumptions.reason: The specification requires risk-based sizing within a 1-2% capital-risk range.

assumptions.choice: No economic-news calendar filter is applied.
assumptions.reason: The fixed OHLCV-only environment contains no economic-news-release data.
